task.title: Fix T10R3-F-001 re-walk crash safety, T10R3-F-002 the ack-route count oracle, T10R3-F-003 the loopback hostname rule
task.description:
Make the RED tests T15 wrote pass, without weakening anything. You did not write those tests and you must not change them: they are the specification for this task. Three defects, found by the independent verification of T10 (attempt 3).

T10R3-F-001 (major). The contact-import re-walk is not crash-safe. `Profile.takeMailboxRewalk()` in apps/cli/src/runtime/profile.ts DELETES the durable position `cli:mailbox-rewalk` before the walk begins; `keepMailboxRewalk()` writes it back only after the page loop returns, or from the catch around it. The whole walk is therefore a window in which the position exists in no durable place, and an interruption inside it — Ctrl-C is enough, and inbound.ts itself names Ctrl-C as a normal interruption — silently and permanently loses the recovery and the message it was requested for.

The orchestrator's intended shape is peek-and-advance rather than take-and-restore: never remove the position before the walk; advance it to the position the walk actually reached; clear it only when the walk reaches the end of the mailbox. At every instant the store must then hold a position at or behind where the walk truly got to, which is the invariant that makes an interruption cost repeated work rather than a lost message. You may choose a different mechanism, but it must satisfy every test, and the invariant above is what the tests are pinning.

The trap you must not fall into, because it is a worse defect than the one you are fixing: delete-before-the-walk was deliberate. The comment on `takeMailboxRewalk` cites finding T6-F-004 — a re-walk position that survives its own SUCCESSFUL walk makes every later poll restart at the same place and reinstates the entire mailbox flooding class this flow exists to close. A green guard test already pins this and it must stay green. Passing the crash-safety tests by never clearing the position is a failure of this task, not a solution to it.

T10R3-F-002 (minor). The ack route still answers a mailbox's lifetime envelope count to a caller who cannot produce a verifying signature: a real `device_id` from a contact card plus a junk signature distinguishes an in-range `read_through` from an out-of-range one, and a binary search recovers the exact count in about 13 requests. Apply the same split T14 already applied to the poll route: validate the SHAPE of `read_through` before authorisation — which is what the existing malformed-shapes test in mailbox_read_mark_test.go demands, that malformed input never answers 500 and never depends on authorisation — and apply the RANGE bound only after `VerifyMessageSignature`. A caller whose signature does not verify then gets one uniform answer because the range check never runs, and `TestAckRefusesAReadThroughAboveAnyPositionTheRelayIssued` stays green because it signs correctly. Do not introduce a special-case uniform error code; the split is the fix.

T10R3-F-003 (minor). `RelayClient` decides loopback with `/^127\./` at apps/cli/src/transport/relayClient.ts:75, which accepts the hostname `127.evil.example` and would serve every relay request to a remote host over plain HTTP. It is unreachable through the CLI today only because config validation runs first at apps/cli/src/commands/cli.ts:210 — a defence in depth that currently is not one. Make `RelayClient` and `parseClientConfig` agree on exactly what loopback means, keeping `127.0.0.1`, `127.9.9.9`, `localhost` and `[::1]` working.
task.scope: apps/cli/src/runtime/profile.ts, apps/cli/src/runtime/inbound.ts, apps/cli/src/transport/relayClient.ts, apps/relay/internal/api/handler/mailbox_handler.go, and whatever else these require. No test files.

acceptance_criteria: Every RED test T15 wrote passes, and every green guard T15 wrote still passes — in particular the T6-F-004 guard that a completed re-walk is not repeated. Report the named result of each.
No test file is modified, at all. Report the SHA-256 of every test file T15 touched, showing it is unchanged from T15's recorded value.
No existing test is weakened, skipped, narrowed or deleted, and no strict Zod schema or Go validation is relaxed.

The re-walk position is never absent from durable storage while a walk that owns it is in flight. State plainly where it is written, where it is cleared, and why no interruption can fall between them.
The F-012 store-identity guarantee is preserved: an ordinary poll with no re-walk pending still leaves the encrypted store byte-identical. Show this rather than asserting it.
The ack fix is the shape/range split, not a special-case error code, and both pre-existing read-mark tests stay green.

The full matrix is green on the resulting tree: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e`, and `go -C apps/relay test ./...` untagged, with `-race` and with `-race -tags relayv2`. Report exact counts and exit codes, and report 0 data races.

A written implementation report at .metaproject/flows/002-2026-09-07-echolet-close-the-flood-class-operator-c/t16-implementation-report.md explaining each change, why the alternative was rejected, and every residual that remains.

context_refs.summary: The RED set that specifies this task, its measured failures, and the two items the orchestrator ruled on.
The independent verification these three findings come from, with the verifier's own reproductions.
How the durable re-walk position and the poll-route shape/range split were introduced; the ack route was not given the same split.
The closure design; §4 states the R-4 rule bounding read_through and the R-5 recovery path the re-walk implements.
Carries the orchestrator's two rulings, including why the re-walk floor must stay local rather than move onto the relay.

constraints: Do NOT modify any test file. The tests are the specification; if you believe a test is wrong, stop and report it rather than editing it.
Do not weaken, skip, narrow or delete any existing test, and do not relax any strict Zod schema or Go validation to obtain green.
Do not pass the crash-safety tests by never clearing the re-walk position — that reinstates finding T6-F-004 and the whole flooding class.

Do not move the re-walk floor onto the relay. The orchestrator rejected that on the merits: the relay is adversary-adjacent, and `contact import` is an offline trust operation that makes no relay request.
Do not print plaintext, ciphertext, store keys, profile keys, private key material or HTTP request bodies into logs or reports.
Every text or symbol search goes through `keryx ctx rg`, never a bare rg or grep; route commands and large logs through `keryx ctx run` / `keryx ctx read`.
Report file identity by SHA-256, never by mtime — files in this tree have been touched with byte-identical content.
Do not edit flow.json or the frozen acceptance-criteria.md.

`bash -lc` on this machine starts Node v22.12.0, which lacks `node:sqlite` and makes packages/session-node fail to collect in a way that looks exactly like broken code. Use the default non-login interpreter, v26.5.0. Report the version you ran on.
